A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SIU3R and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The retained material can be matched reliably despite appendix expansion and figure relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original ScanNet reconstruction and segmentation experiments, component ablations, and qualitative editing results, including supplementary comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds multi-view experiments, depth-baseline comparisons, and qualitative results on cellphone-captured scenes.

M1.justification: v1 restricts inputs to two views. v2 Appendix C extends cross-attention so each view attends to concatenated tokens from all other views, enabling additional view-count variants. This is a localized architectural adaptation; the query decoder, lifting procedure, and mutual-benefit components remain.

E1.justification: v2 Appendix E.1 adds evaluation on newly collected handheld-cellphone images, illustrated with indoor real-world scenes in Figure II. ScanNet evaluation, COCO pretraining, and the reconstruction and segmentation task coverage are retained.

E2.justification: v2 Appendix D, Table IV adds evaluated DUSt3R, MASt3R, and VGGT baselines, introducing a distinct class of point-based geometry methods into the depth comparison. This substantially broadens competitive coverage beyond rendering and segmentation pipelines. The original comparator sets remain.

E3.justification: Appendix C adds separately retrained 2-, 4-, 6-, and 8-view configurations, with accuracy, inference time, and training/inference memory measurements. Appendix E.1 adds zero-shot cellphone-image testing. The original ScanNet split, 1,860 evaluation pairs, metrics, and stated training budget remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a focused view-count sensitivity study examining accuracy and computational cost, plus qualitative generalization cases on cellphone captures. The original mutual-benefit ablations and early-versus-late aggregation analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-seed counts, confidence intervals, standard deviations, or statistical significance tests. The new view-count variants are distinct configurations, not repeated-run uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: Original result tables remain unchanged, but substantial new scaling and comparative findings appear. Table III reports PSNR increasing from 25.96 with two views to 26.65 with eight, alongside training memory increasing from approximately 24 GB to 77.5 GB. Table IV newly shows all three point-based baselines ahead on depth accuracy, including VGGT AbsRel 0.052 versus SIU3R 0.074. Figure II adds real-world qualitative outcomes.

T1.justification: The existing objectives, query-matching mathematics, depth-continuity reasoning, and overlap definition are retained. v2 spells out the previously cited mask-loss decomposition without establishing a mathematical correction or new theoretical result. Neither version contains formal proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same central claims: alignment-free joint reconstruction and understanding, unified queries, mutual benefits, and state-of-the-art performance. Adding the word 'segmentation' clarifies existing task terminology rather than redefining the contribution.

C2.justification: v1's two-view restriction and proposed video extension are replaced by a limitation concerning training-data scale and broader-domain generalization; the annotation-noise limitation remains. New appendix discussion attributes multi-view gains to reduced geometric uncertainty and explains depth and speed differences against point-based methods through supervision, training data, post-processing, and model size.

D1.justification: v2 discloses mask-loss components and weights of 5, 5, and 2, specifies which existing baselines were retrained and that LSeg used pretrained weights, and reports SIU3R's 650M parameters. These clarify implementation without establishing changes to the original experiments. The LSM training-duration comparison is removed; existing preprocessing and release statements remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds the VGGT citation and expands positioning against VGGT and the already cited DUSt3R and MASt3R, discussing task support, supervision, and computational requirements. The related-work section and central alignment-free novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The main narrative is largely retained, with localized loss and baseline explanations, revised limitations, updated affiliations and conference text, and acknowledgements. New Appendices C and D shift the existing visualization appendix from C to E, without extensive rewriting of retained material.

P2.justification: v2 adds Appendix Tables III and IV and a real-world Figure II. Existing visual results are retained, with Figure 4 relocated, some figures resized, and appendix figures renumbered. These are limited additions and layout adjustments rather than a broad visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v2 tests an extension beyond v1's explicit two-view restriction, adds stronger depth comparisons that expose SIU3R's geometry tradeoff, and improves reproducibility through loss and baseline-training disclosures. These are useful gains, while the central experimental evidence remains unchanged. The added real-world evidence is qualitative, and timing reports across Tables II and IV are not explicitly reconciled, limiting the strength of the expanded validation.
